meta.purpose: Known-answer vectors for the Sanctum Shamir example tool. See SPEC.md section 5 for the exact algorithm.

conventions.indices: All 'subsets' are 0-based indices into the vector's own 'shares' array. Each subset, passed to combine() in the listed order, must return the secret.
conventions.rngHex: The exact bytes the deterministic split must consume, in order, as ONE continuous stream. For 'ss1': first randomBytes(4) for the set id, then randomBytes(P*(k-1)). For 'plain': only randomBytes(L*(k-1)). Feeding these bytes through options.randomBytes must reproduce 'shares' exactly.
conventions.testRng: rngHex was produced by concatenating SHA-256(utf8('secret:'+vectorId) || u32be(counter)) for counter 0,1,2,... and truncating. Builders do not need this; they only replay rngHex.

producedBy.reference: gen/ref.py: pure Python 3, GF(2^8) multiply by shift-and-xor over x^8+x^4+x^3+x+1 (no tables copied from any library).
producedBy.privyCrossCheck: Every 'plain' vector and every raw share was re-combined with the real npm package shamir-secret-sharing@0.0.4 (Apache-2.0) in Node; see vectors 'crossChecks' below and gen/verify_privy.mjs.
producedBy.ssss: 'classic' vectors come from the real ssss 0.5 binary compiled from source, then re-derived by an independent Python model.

gf256.polynomial: x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 (0x11b), the AES field. Generator 3 has order 255.
gf256.note: mulTableSha256 is SHA-256 of the 65536-byte table T[a*256+b] = mul(a,b). Privy's 0xe5-generator log/exp tables give the same products (checked for all 255x255 nonzero pairs).

meta.produced: Shares from the real ssss-split 0.5 binary (random), secrets recovered by the real ssss-combine 0.5 AND by gen/classic.py (independent Python model); all three agree for every listed subset. -Q silences warnings. ASCII mode output is lossy for non-printable bytes, so vectors use printable ASCII or hex mode.
meta.combineRule: ssss-combine needs exactly t shares; classic.py uses exactly the listed subset (size t). Extra shares are not used.
